cell_type: Allogeneic bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy
regulatory_status: FDA approved 2024-12-18 (first FDA-approved MSC product for any indication); launched US market March 2025
price_basis: Company-set wholesale acquisition cost (WAC), i.e. an actual list price, not a value-based recommendation
dosing_regimen: Twice-weekly IV infusions for 4 weeks (8 infusions total); full course therefore approx. $1.55 million
source: BioWorld (T. Sami, reporting Mesoblast's launch pricing); Managed Healthcare Executive (FDA orphan drug exclusivity coverage, states the $194,000 WAC per-infusion figure and the ~$1.55M full-course total)
note: Closest real-world market-price comparator found for an approved, off-the-shelf allogeneic cell therapy in an immune-mediated (non-oncology) indication -- not Treg-specific (MSC, not Tr1/Treg) and not Crohn's, but the best available analog for 'what does an approved allogeneic cell product actually get priced at'. Not used as a model parameter; kept as Discussion-section market context alongside the ten Ham-derived $19,916.75/dose acquisition-cost estimate (model_tenham_derived_treg_dose_cost.csv), which is a manufacturing-COGS-based build-up, not a market price -- the two figures answer different questions and should not be conflated.

company: Atara Biotherapeutics (Pierre Fabre holds EU/UK commercialisation rights)
indication: EBV-positive post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease (EBV+ PTLD), relapsed/refractory
regulatory_status: EU/UK approved (as Ebvallo); NOT FDA approved -- second Complete Response Letter received 2026-01-09/12, US status unresolved as of this note
price_basis: ICER (Institute for Clinical and Economic Review) value-based price recommendation, i.e. 'what price would make this cost-effective' -- NOT a company-set list price, since the product is not commercially priced in the US
dosing_regimen: Not itself Treg/Tr1 (EBV-specific effector T-cell, not a regulatory/tolerogenic cell product); included as a second allogeneic-cell-therapy pricing data point, methodologically closer to this project's own EJP framing since ICER's number IS a cost-effectiveness-derived price
source: Managed Healthcare Executive, reporting ICER's evidence report: 'a rating of A ... would be cost-effective if priced between $143,900 and $273,700 [per treatment cycle]'
note: The $143,900-$273,700 range IS the price_usd_per_unit for this row (two-sided, not a point estimate) -- left the single-value column blank rather than force a range into a scalar field; see this note for the actual figures. Directly relevant precedent: this is another US HTA body computing a cost-effectiveness-justified price for an allogeneic cell therapy, i.e. functionally the same exercise as this project's own EJP (Section 9.1) -- worth citing methodologically, not just for the dollar figure.
